planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in average, well-drained soil; a compact sport of the low-spreading Abelia x grandiflora Prostrata, Silver Anniversary keeps a tidy mounded shape with little pruning.

directions: Grown chiefly for its bright green leaves edged in silvery cream, carried on contrasting deep red stems that show best where a few hours of direct sun reach the plant each day. Clusters of fragrant, white flowers tinged pink open in the leaf axils and at stem tips from late spring into fall, drawing bees, butterflies, and hummingbirds without overshadowing the foliage display. Its dense, rounded, multi-stemmed habit stays low enough for foundation plantings or a low informal hedge without frequent shearing. Established plants tolerate clay soil, heat, and short dry spells; remove any plain-green reverted shoots promptly since they grow faster than the variegated wood.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in average, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; brighter light intensifies the pink-and-gold new growth.

directions: Sold under the trademark Sunshine Daydream, this abelia is grown for tricolor foliage that opens dark pink on new growth before softening into a marbled mix of golden yellow, pink, and green that shifts through the season. Fragrant white flowers brushed with rose pink open from spring through fall on a rounded, well-branched frame, adding a light floral layer to the foliage show and drawing butterflies and hummingbirds. It suits foundation plantings, mixed borders, and large containers where its color can be seen up close. Like other glossy abelias it is deer resistant and tolerates heat, humidity, and drought once established, needing only a light shaping after the heaviest spring bloom flush.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in average, well-drained soil; bred from a cross of Edward Goucher and Abelia chinensis, it is notably cold hardy for an abelia and can be grown into zone 5b.

directions: Valued for showy raspberry-red calyces that persist and color the plant long after the fragrant, pink-purple tubular flowers themselves have dropped, giving an unusually long season of color from a compact, upright, arching frame. New growth emerges glossy red before aging to dark green, and heavy bloom runs from May into September, drawing steady butterfly and hummingbird traffic. Its more compact size and superior cold hardiness compared with typical Abelia x grandiflora cultivars make it a good choice for gardeners at the northern edge of abelia country. Once established it needs no supplemental irrigation and only a light shaping cut after the main flush to keep its habit tidy.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in average, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; a fountain-like habit suits foundation plantings and flower beds.

directions: Sold under the trademark Sunny Anniversary, this is the only widely marketed abelia with yellow flowers, each bloom opening buttery yellow with a deep pink throat and freckled yellow center. Large, fragrant flowers begin in midsummer and continue in flushes to frost on a soft, arching, fountain-shaped shrub, drawing bees, butterflies, and hummingbirds through the peak of the pollinator season. Leathery, dark green leaves persist through winter in mild climates, giving structure to the border once bloom has finished. It tolerates dry soil and part shade with minimal care once established, needing only a light shaping cut after the first bloom flush if a tighter form is wanted.
